newsitem.title: USA: US agency debt issuance $128 bln Jan-Jul 1996 -PSA.
newsitem.headline: US agency debt issuance $128 bln Jan-Jul 1996 -PSA.

text.p: Issuance of U.S. federal agency debt securities rose more than 30 percent in the first seven months of 1996 against the same period last year, according to the Public Securities Association (PSA).
Debt issued by federal agencies or government-sponsored enterprises totaled $128 billion through July 1996, up from $98 billion in the same time frame last year, PSA said.
The PSA report identified the top five issuers.
The Federal National Mortgage Association, with $59.8 billion of new securities, was the top issuer, PSA said.
The Federal Home Loan Bank System ranked second with $25.2 billion in debt securities, according to PSA.
The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp was the third-largest issuer with $20.5 billion during the period, PSA said.
The Farm Credit System placed fourth with $16.7 billion of new issues and the Student Loan Marketing Association came in fifth with $3.1 billion, it said.
PSA is the bond market trade association.
